correctness.rationale: An exact polar-side parameterization and Jacobian give uniform radial and density expansions. The squared chord cosine law, combined with an event-localization bound, justifies dominated convergence to the explicit two-variable sublevel measure. The sole even minimum and two odd minima have exact first-order polyhedral cones, yielding 1/2 and 16/9 onset coefficients. Uniform boundedness of radial deficits proves the common 2 sqrt(t) envelope. Standalone code checks exact rational wedge factors and 12 finite-n quadratures; finite checks are diagnostic only.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies a singular geometric-probability transition from polygonal diameter localization to circular antipodal abundance. It identifies a sharp parity-induced onset gap and two explicit quadratic onset constants alongside the universal large-scale square-root behavior. These are natural implications of refining regular polygons, neither a trivial shape substitution nor a stand-alone routine integral.
